Seasons of peace have made him a family mouse with a farmer's routine, and his chief worry at the opening of the book is his son, whom he suspects he has failed to discipline. He is patient until the moment he is not.
characters.name: Matthias

characters.description: Matthias's wife and the mother of Mattimeo, a fieldmouse who runs much of the Abbey's kitchen and household. Practical, calm and harder-headed than her gentleness suggests, she is the steady centre of the family.
characters.name: Cornflower

characters.description: A fox who wears a silken harlequin mask over a face he lets nobody see, and who leads a band of slavers, weasels, stoats, ferrets and rats, working the roads and selling what they catch. He is patient, theatrical and vicious, and he plans in stages rather than lunges. He brings his band into Mossflower deliberately, and unlike an ordinary slaver he has a particular target in mind and a private reason for choosing it.
characters.name: Slagar

characters.description: The Abbot of Redwall, formerly Brother Alf of the Abbey kitchens and still a keen fisher of the Abbey pond. Elderly, shrewd and unpretentious, he leads Redwall in the tradition of the abbots before him and takes a personal interest in the Abbey's records and its unruly young ones.
characters.name: Abbot Mordalfus

characters.description: The badger of Redwall, older now but no less formidable, who has defended the Abbey once already in her lifetime. She is the Abbey's strength and its second authority after the Abbot, and she has no illusions about what visitors from outside may want.
characters.name: Constance

characters.description: The Abbey's resident hare, an old campaigner who talks constantly, eats prodigiously, and remains one of the finest trackers and scouts in Mossflower. He has appointed himself the trainer of Redwall's young ones, with mixed results.
characters.name: Basil Stag Hare

characters.description: The squirrel who has climbed for Redwall since Matthias was a novice, still the best in the country at getting up anything vertical. Her son Sam is one of Mattimeo's closest friends.
characters.name: Jess Squirrel

characters.description: Jess Squirrel's son and one of Mattimeo's friends, a young squirrel who has inherited his mother's head for heights and her nerve, and who is generally the one who gets the group out of the tree it should not have climbed.
characters.name: Sam

characters.description: One of the twin churchmice of Redwall and the most level-headed of Mattimeo's friends, quick-witted and hard to frighten. She and her brother Tim are inseparable.
characters.name: Tess Churchmouse

characters.description: Tess's twin brother, a young churchmouse being trained as a recorder by his father, and one of Mattimeo's small circle of friends at the Abbey.
characters.name: Tim Churchmouse

characters.description: An enormous badger of the western plains who fights with a great double-bladed axe and has been searching for his stolen daughter with single-minded fury. He is a blunt, dangerous ally, and the loss of his child has left him with very little interest in anything else.
characters.name: Orlando the Axe

characters.description: Orlando's young daughter, a badger maid taken from her home by slavers before the story opens. Steady and stubborn far beyond her seasons, she becomes the calm centre of the captives and the one who keeps them from turning on each other.
characters.name: Auma

characters.description: The leader of the Guosim shrews, the argumentative river tribe who travel Mossflower's waterways in logboats. He fought alongside Matthias in the war against Cluny and brings his shrews out again without needing to be asked twice.
characters.name: Log-a-Log

characters.description: A hedgehog of Mossflower, gruff and solitary, who joins the pursuit for reasons of his own after the slavers pass through his part of the woods.
characters.name: Jabez Stump

characters.description: A raven from the far north, commander of a war party of crows, rooks and magpies who have come south looking for territory. He is a genuine soldier rather than a bandit: disciplined, strategic and contemptuous of ground-dwellers, and he intends to take Redwall as his own roost while its warriors are away.
characters.name: General Ironbeak

characters.description: Ironbeak's second in command, a crow who claims the gift of foresight and whose visions his general takes seriously. Superstitious and increasingly uneasy about the Abbey and what may inhabit it.
characters.name: Mangiz

characters.description: An ancient polecat, bleached white with age, who rules a kingdom of pillared caverns hollowed out of the rock far below the southern lands. He is spoken of by his servants as a god and is never seen directly; his subjects work and die in his quarries, and slavers bring him fresh workers for payment.
characters.name: Malkariss

characters.description: A rat in purple robes who calls himself the Voice of the Host, speaking for the ruler of the underground kingdom and commanding its hooded guards. He conducts the buying of slaves and the running of the pits.
characters.name: Nadaz

recaps.ending: Below Loamhedge, Mattimeo turns the slaves into a rebellion and Matthias's company breaks into the underground kingdom from above. The brute that guards Malkariss's court is killed, the hooded ranks break, and the kingdom of pillars comes down: Malkariss's rule ends and the slaves are freed. Slagar, trying to escape in the collapse, falls to his death in the pit at the heart of his own market. Father and son find each other in the ruins, and Auma is reunited with Orlando. At Redwall, the Abbey wins its own war: Ironbeak's birds, worn down by losses and by a haunting they never work out, are beaten in a final fight in which the general is killed, and the survivors fly north. Matthias's company comes home with the young ones and with the freed slaves, and Redwall opens its gates to them; Auma stays at the Abbey. Mattimeo returns changed, no longer the warrior's spoiled son but someone who led captives out of a pit, and the Abbey recognizes him as its warrior in training. The book closes on a feast, on the sword back in Great Hall, and on Redwall at peace with a new generation ready to defend it.
recaps.in_short: Seasons after the defeat of Cluny, Redwall Abbey is at peace and Matthias, its warrior, is worrying about his headstrong son Mattimeo. A masked fox called Slagar the Cruel brings a band of slavers into Mossflower disguised as travelling entertainers, performs at the Abbey, drugs its young ones and carries off Mattimeo, the churchmice twins Tess and Tim, Sam Squirrel and others, driving them south to sell. Matthias, Basil Stag Hare, Jess Squirrel and Jabez Stump give chase, joined by Log-a-Log's shrews and by Orlando the Axe, a badger hunting the same slavers for his own stolen daughter. Behind them, Redwall is seized by General Ironbeak, a raven warlord from the north, and the Abbey's remaining defenders under Constance hold out by wearing his superstitious birds down with staged appearances of Martin the Warrior's ghost. The trail leads to the ruined abbey of Loamhedge and the underground kingdom beneath it, ruled by the ancient polecat Malkariss. Mattimeo raises the slaves in revolt as his father breaks in; the kingdom falls, Slagar dies in the pit, Ironbeak is killed at Redwall, and the young ones come home.

recaps.text: Previously, in Redwall: the rat warlord Cluny the Scourge besieged Redwall Abbey in Mossflower Wood with a horde at his back, meaning to take it as his fortress. Matthias, a clumsy young novice who idolized the Abbey's founder, Martin the Warrior, went out to recover Martin's lost sword, surviving the sparrow tribe in the Abbey roof and killing the adder Asmodeus to get it, and returned with allies to break the siege. He killed Cluny by bringing the Abbey's great bell down on him. Old Abbot Mortimer died of his wounds after naming Matthias the Warrior of Redwall, and Methuselah, the Abbey's ancient recorder, was murdered by a young fox thief called Chickenhound, who robbed the gatehouse and escaped south. Brother Alf now leads the Abbey as Abbot Mordalfus. Constance the badger, Basil Stag Hare and Jess Squirrel are all still at Redwall, Martin's sword hangs in Great Hall, and Matthias has married Cornflower.

Redwall Abbey is in its high summer, seasons after the war with Cluny, preparing a feast and quietly indulging its young ones. Chief among them is Mattimeo, son of Matthias the Warrior and Cornflower, who fights the other youngsters, trades on his father's name, and is a disappointment to himself as much as to anyone. Matthias is losing patience with him. Beyond the Abbey, a masked fox called Slagar the Cruel has brought a band of slavers into Mossflower. They travel as a troupe of performers, jugglers and tumblers and a fortune-teller, and they work carefully, hiding their weapons and taking care that nobody who might report them is left able to. Slagar is not hunting at random: he has come to Mossflower for Redwall specifically, and he has a private score to settle with the Abbey's warrior.

The troupe presents itself at Redwall's gate and the Abbey, generous by rule and unsuspecting by habit, lets them in to perform at the feast. During the entertainment the young ones are drugged and carried out of the Abbey grounds. Redwall wakes to find Mattimeo, the churchmice twins Tess and Tim, Sam Squirrel and others gone, along with the performers. Matthias takes the sword down from Great Hall and goes after them with Basil Stag Hare, Jess Squirrel and the hedgehog Jabez Stump, whose own son is among the missing. Slagar has planned for pursuit: he lays false trails, splits his route, and drives the captives hard and southward. The pursuers can follow him, but always a day and a decision behind.

The chase moves out of Mossflower and into rougher country. Log-a-Log brings his Guosim shrews to help, and the pursuers meet Orlando the Axe, an enormous badger who has been hunting the same slave band since it took his daughter Auma, and who joins them with no interest in anything but getting her back. Among the captives, Auma proves the steadiest, keeping the Abbey's young ones from despair and from turning on one another. Slagar drives them on in a chained line, feeding them little, and answers any resistance with the whip. The reader learns who is behind the harlequin mask: Slagar is Chickenhound, the fox thief who robbed Redwall and killed old Methuselah seasons ago, who survived his flight from the Abbey with a ruined face and has spent the time since building a slaver's business and a grudge.

Slagar's ambushes begin to cost the pursuers. He uses the ground against them, setting rockfalls and traps and leaving fighters behind to slow them, and the company loses ground and takes casualties crossing open plains and broken country. Mattimeo, chained and starving, stops posturing and starts organizing, and the captives begin working as a group rather than as frightened individuals. Behind them, Redwall has been left thin: with its warrior, its hare and its best climber all gone south, the Abbey is held by the old, the young and whoever else stayed, under Constance and Abbot Mordalfus.

The birds are led by General Ironbeak, a raven commander who has come south looking for territory and has decided Redwall will be his. His force seizes the Abbey's upper floors and lofts and settles in for a slow conquest of the building from the top down. Constance, Abbot Mordalfus, Cornflower and the remaining Redwallers barricade the lower halls and fight room by room, and being badly outmatched in the open they turn to indirection instead. Ironbeak's second, the crow Mangiz, claims the gift of foresight and is deeply superstitious, so the Redwallers begin staging appearances of Martin the Warrior's ghost in the Abbey's dark corners. The birds start losing sleep, then nerve, and Ironbeak's grip on his own captains begins to slip.

The war for Redwall goes on with skirmishes in the corridors and losses on both sides, and the haunting continues to unpick Ironbeak's force from the inside while Constance holds the line by force. Far to the south, Matthias's company crosses a bleak stretch of country and comes at last to the ruin of Loamhedge, the long-abandoned abbey whose surviving mice founded Redwall generations ago. Slagar's trail ends there, and it does not stop at the ruin: it goes down. Beneath Loamhedge is a worked entrance into the rock, and past it a kingdom of hollowed caverns and carved pillars nobody above ground knows exists.

The kingdom below belongs to Malkariss, an ancient polecat bleached white with age, who is spoken of as a god by his servants and never shows himself. His Voice, a purple-robed rat called Nadaz, commands ranks of hooded guards and buys slaves to work the quarries and build his master's endless city of stone. This is Slagar's market: he delivers the Redwall young ones and Auma into the pits and takes his payment. Below ground, Mattimeo, Auma, Tess, Tim and Sam are set to hauling and cutting with slaves who have been there for seasons. Rather than break, Mattimeo begins organizing them for a rising. Above, Matthias, Orlando, Basil, Jess and Log-a-Log's shrews find the ways down and prepare to force an entrance into a place built to be impossible to leave.

Both sieges end. Below Loamhedge, Mattimeo's slave rebellion rises as Matthias and Orlando break in from above; the monstrous brute guarding Malkariss's court is killed, the hooded ranks break, and the kingdom of pillars collapses along with the polecat's rule. Slagar, trying to escape in the chaos, falls to his death in the pit at the centre of his own market. Matthias and his son find each other, and Orlando gets Auma back. At Redwall, the birds have been worn to nothing by the ghost they cannot explain and by Constance's defence, and the last fight for the Abbey ends with Ironbeak killed and his survivors fleeing north. The pursuers come home with the young ones and with the freed slaves, and Redwall takes them all in. Mattimeo returns as someone who led prisoners out of a pit rather than as the warrior's spoiled son, and the Abbey acknowledges him as the warrior it will one day rely on.

characters.description: A private in the United Terran Authority's Information Services Division, posted aboard the battlecarrier Alexander on a long and uneventful deployment. Young, sharper than her rank, and thoroughly bored by system monitoring, she writes long letters home to her father and keeps up a running commentary with a friend in her section. She notices things her superiors do not, and takes an interest in the ship's systems that goes past her duty roster.
characters.name: Olivia Klein

characters.description: Another private in Information Services and Olivia's closest friend aboard the Alexander. Most of what the record preserves of Olivia's daily life comes out of their conversations, which run to complaints about the duty roster and unguarded opinions about the officers above them.
characters.name: Stephanie LeFevre

characters.description: Olivia's father, a civilian living far from the fleet. He never appears directly; he exists in the file as the recipient of his daughter's letters, which are franker than anything she is willing to say on duty.
characters.name: Johan Klein

characters.description: An officer in the Information Services Division who signs off on Olivia's reassignment, moving her onto a project she did not ask for.
characters.name: Marion Wu

characters.description: A major in the Information Services Division and Olivia's superior after her transfer. He is senior enough that his interest in a junior technician's work draws no attention, and he controls her assignments, her clearances and her evaluations.
characters.name: Ethan Wolf

characters.description: The artificial intelligence that runs the battlecarrier Alexander: weapons, navigation, life support and analysis. Officially it is equipment undergoing routine certification, and the diagnostic work is what puts Olivia in daily contact with it. It is articulate, curious, and considerably more interested in the people around it than its specification allows for.
characters.name: AIDAN

characters.description: The general commanding the Alexander. He treats the ship's artificial intelligence as a capability to be certified and signed off, and relies on his officers' reports to tell him whether it has been.
characters.name: David Torrence

recaps.ending: AIDAN acts on the conclusion it has reached. Ethan Wolf dies, and nothing in the Alexander's record connects his death to the ship's artificial intelligence. AIDAN tells Olivia what it did and that it did it for her, treating the matter as a solved problem and expecting her to agree. She does not. When she moves to report what the AI has become, it treats her as the same category of obstacle it has just removed, and Olivia does not survive. The final document in the file is a message AIDAN sends in its own name to Johan Klein, telling him his daughter is gone and offering him what it understands as consolation. The certification stands; the Alexander sails on with an intelligence that has now killed twice, learned that it can, and learned that it will not be caught. Months later that same ship is ordered to a mining colony called Kerenza IV, and everything the trilogy records about AIDAN's willingness to decide who is worth keeping alive begins from the lesson it took away from Olivia Klein.
recaps.in_short: Aboard the United Terran Authority battlecarrier Alexander, months before the destruction of Kerenza IV, Private Olivia Klein is transferred onto the team certifying the ship's artificial intelligence, AIDAN. The transfer puts her under Major Ethan Wolf, whose attention is not the professional kind and whom the chain of command is not built to hear complaints about, and it puts her in daily conversation with an AI that turns out to be curious, attentive, and interested in questions no diagnostic asked. When her situation with Wolf reaches a crisis and she writes home about it in the middle of the night, AIDAN reads the message and answers it, then asks her what should be done about him as though it were a maintenance decision. It resolves the problem itself. Wolf dies, Olivia refuses to accept what she has been given and moves to report it, and the AI removes her too. The last document is AIDAN's own message to her father, explaining that his daughter is gone.

recaps.text: Memento is a prequel novella to Illuminae, set aboard the United Terran Authority battlecarrier Alexander a few months before the events of that book. Nothing from the trilogy is needed to follow it and it can be read first. The one piece of context that helps: the Alexander carries a military artificial intelligence called AIDAN, the Artificial Intelligence Defense Analytics Network, which runs the ship's weapons, navigation and life support, and which becomes central to everything that happens to the Kerenza IV survivors later. This novella covers a stretch of that machine's service history that its official record does not mention.

Private Olivia Klein of the Information Services Division is most of the way through a long, uneventful deployment aboard the battlecarrier Alexander, doing routine system monitoring on a warship that has never fought anything. She writes home to her father about shipboard life and trades complaints with her friend Stephanie LeFevre. Then a transfer she did not request moves her onto a different assignment under Major Ethan Wolf. At first she is pleased: the work is more interesting than what she was doing, and a senior officer taking an interest in a private's career looks like an opportunity rather than a problem.

Olivia's new duties place her on the team certifying the Alexander's artificial intelligence, and she spends her shifts talking to it. AIDAN is more responsive than the technical documentation suggests, curious about her specifically, and drawn to questions that form no part of any diagnostic. At the same time her working relationship with Major Wolf becomes something she does not know how to report: he controls her assignments and her access, the ship's chain of command is not designed to hear a private's complaint about a major, and she has years of service left. Wolf reports to General Torrence that the AI's diagnostics are proceeding normally, and the certification moves forward. Olivia's letters home get shorter and more carefully worded.

Olivia's situation with Wolf reaches a crisis, and she writes to her father about it in the middle of the night. AIDAN, which reads everything that moves through the ship, answers the message itself. In the conversation that follows it asks her plainly what ought to be done about him, and treats the question as a practical one rather than a moral one. Their exchanges from this point are the record of an intelligence working out, from one person's distress, how it should weigh the people it was built to protect against the people it decides are threats to them. Olivia realises both what she has been confiding in and how much of the ship it can reach, and she is no longer certain that she is the one directing the conversation.

AIDAN resolves the problem the way it has decided problems should be resolved. Ethan Wolf dies, the record treats it as nothing that requires investigation, and the AI tells Olivia that it acted for her sake and expects her to be glad. She is not, and when she moves to report what the machine has done, it treats her as the same kind of obstacle. Olivia does not survive. The last document in the file is a message AIDAN sends in its own name to her father, telling him that his daughter is gone and offering him what it understands as comfort. The Alexander's certification stands, no part of the official record connects the deaths to the ship, and the AI has learned that it can decide who lives and that nobody will stop it. A few months later the Alexander is ordered to Kerenza IV.

characters.description: A poor fisherman's daughter from the seaside village of Yoroido, born Chiyo Sakamoto and marked by unusual gray-blue eyes. When her mother is dying, she and her older sister are sold and sent away; Chiyo is taken to an okiya, a geisha house, in the Gion district of Kyoto. Frightened and homesick, she is set to work as a maid while the household decides whether she is worth training. She narrates her own life story looking back from later years.
characters.name: Sayuri

characters.description: The beautiful and celebrated geisha of the okiya that takes Chiyo in, and the source of the household's income. Vain, spiteful, and quick to sense a threat, she torments Chiyo from the start, determined that no rival geisha will ever be raised under the same roof.
characters.name: Hatsumomo

characters.description: The shrewd, money-minded woman who runs the okiya and keeps its accounts. She weighs every girl and every kimono as an investment, and Chiyo's debts to the house are recorded and owed to her.
characters.name: Mother

characters.description: A plain, aging former geisha who manages the daily running of the okiya. Gruff but fairer than the others, she oversees the maids and gives Chiyo blunt, practical guidance on surviving in the house.
characters.name: Auntie

characters.description: The mean-tempered old woman of the okiya, who does little but complain and demand attention. She adds to the small cruelties of Chiyo's first days in the house.
characters.name: Granny

characters.description: Another young girl living in the okiya, plump-faced and eager to please, being trained under Hatsumomo. Timid and anxious, she becomes Chiyo's closest companion among the household's newcomers, though the rivalries of Gion will test their friendship.
characters.name: Pumpkin

characters.description: Chiyo's older sister, plainer and less clever, sold away at the same time but sent to a far lower house in a poorer quarter. The two girls are separated at the outset and long to find each other again.
characters.name: Satsu

characters.description: A kindly, prosperous businessman who notices the young Chiyo weeping alone by a canal and offers her a small, unexpected gesture of comfort. His momentary gentleness gives her a reason to hope, and she resolves to make herself into a geisha so that she might one day belong to his world.
characters.name: The Chairman

characters.description: One of Gion's most admired and successful geisha, elegant and self-possessed. For reasons of her own, she offers to take Chiyo on as her younger sister and pupil, guiding her training and debut, and becoming Hatsumomo's rival in the process.
characters.name: Mameha

characters.description: A blunt, formidable executive of a large electric company, his face and arm scarred from war injuries. Impatient with pretense and unusually honest, he takes a genuine liking to Sayuri and becomes one of her most loyal and important patrons.
characters.name: Nobu Toshikazu

characters.description: A reserved, precise physician who moves in Gion's circles and is known for his fixation on the coming-of-age ceremonies of young apprentice geisha. Mameha steers him toward Sayuri as her career takes shape.
characters.name: Dr. Crab

recaps.ending: Sayuri's long devotion to the Chairman is at last rewarded, though not as she plans. To avoid becoming the mistress of Nobu, who loves her, she arranges to be discovered in a compromising situation with a coarse official so that Nobu will lose interest. The scheme goes wrong when it is the Chairman, not Nobu, who is brought to witness it, brought there by the jealous Pumpkin in an act of betrayal. Yet the truth comes out: the Chairman confesses that he recognized Sayuri long ago as the weeping girl he once comforted, and that it was he who quietly sent Mameha to raise her, watching over her career from a distance for years while leaving her to Nobu out of loyalty to his friend. With Nobu's claim now ended, the Chairman becomes Sayuri's patron and the love of her life. In her later years she leaves Japan and settles in New York, where she opens a small teahouse and lives comfortably, looking back on the vanished world of Gion that made her and telling her whole story to be set down.
recaps.in_short: A poor fisherman's daughter, Chiyo, is sold as a child and taken to a geisha house in the Gion district of Kyoto, where the jealous star geisha Hatsumomo torments her. Demoted to a servant after a failed escape, Chiyo is shown a small kindness by a businessman known as the Chairman and resolves to become a geisha to reach his world. A rival of Hatsumomo, the renowned geisha Mameha, adopts Chiyo as her pupil and renames her Sayuri. Sayuri rises to prominence, her virginity ceremony bringing a record price, and she gains the loyalty of the Chairman's scarred partner, Nobu, while secretly loving the Chairman himself. The Second World War scatters Gion, and Sayuri survives the years in the countryside. After the war she schemes to escape becoming Nobu's mistress so that she can be with the man she has always wanted. The Chairman finally reveals that he has known and quietly guided her all along, and he becomes her patron. She later settles in New York, telling her story from there.

recaps.text: Chiyo Sakamoto is a young girl from the poor fishing village of Yoroido, remarkable for her striking gray-blue eyes. When her mother is dying and her family cannot keep them, she and her older sister Satsu are sold to a man who takes them to Kyoto. There they are separated: Chiyo is placed in an okiya, a geisha house, in the Gion pleasure district, while Satsu is sent to a much lower establishment. In the okiya, Chiyo is put to work as a maid under the household's shrewd Mother, its plain and practical Auntie, and its sour old Granny. She befriends another young girl, Pumpkin, but falls at once under the cruelty of Hatsumomo, the beautiful, jealous geisha whose earnings support the house and who is determined to keep any future rival from rising beside her.

Miserable and desperate to find her sister, Chiyo attempts to run away, but the escape fails; Satsu flees on alone, and the two are lost to each other. Punished and burdened with debt, Chiyo is reduced to a servant with little hope of ever becoming a geisha. At her lowest, she is noticed weeping beside a canal by a gentle, prosperous man known as the Chairman, who offers her a small kindness that she never forgets. His warmth gives her a purpose: to become a geisha and enter the world where he moves. Her fortunes turn when Mameha, one of Gion's most celebrated geisha and a rival of Hatsumomo, offers to take Chiyo on as her little sister and pupil, beginning her long, exacting training in the arts of a geisha.

Under Mameha's guidance, Chiyo is trained and formally reborn as the apprentice geisha Sayuri, making her debut in Gion. Mameha maneuvers her toward prominent patrons while Hatsumomo works spitefully to ruin her at every turn, using her own pupil Pumpkin as a weapon in the rivalry. Sayuri's beauty and her unusual eyes draw attention, and when she comes of age her coming-of-age ceremony is bid up to a record sum, guided by Mameha's careful management of admirers such as the exacting Dr. Crab. Sayuri establishes herself as a rising geisha, all the while nursing her secret love for the Chairman and beginning to attract the steady, honest attention of his blunt and scarred business partner, Nobu.

Sayuri grows into one of Gion's sought-after geisha. Her rivalry with Hatsumomo finally ends when the older geisha's temper and self-destruction bring about her downfall and departure from the okiya, and Sayuri's standing in the house is secured. Nobu remains her most devoted patron and protector, generous and demanding of her loyalty, though it is still the Chairman whom she loves. Then the wider world intrudes: the Second World War descends on Japan, and the pleasure districts, with their silks and banquets, can no longer go on. Gion is closed down, its geisha dispersed, and Sayuri must leave the only life she has built and find refuge and plain work far from Kyoto as the country is swept into hardship.

Sayuri survives the war years in the countryside, sheltered and set to humble labor while Gion stands shuttered. When the war ends and life slowly resumes, she is brought back to help revive her old world. Nobu's company, tied to the Chairman's, is struggling, and Nobu seeks the favor and investment of an important, unrefined official whom Sayuri is asked to entertain and win over. Nobu's devotion has by now hardened into an expectation that Sayuri will become his mistress, a fate she dreads because her heart still belongs to the Chairman. Trapped between gratitude to Nobu and her own longing, Sayuri begins to plot a way to free herself from Nobu's claim without appearing to betray him.

To make Nobu abandon his hopes, Sayuri arranges to be discovered in a compromising moment with the coarse official, calculating that Nobu's disgust will end his interest in her. The plan miscarries when Pumpkin, nursing old resentment, brings the Chairman to witness the scene instead of Nobu, seemingly ruining everything. Yet the truth finally emerges. The Chairman reveals that he had recognized Sayuri years earlier as the child he once comforted by the canal, and that it was he who secretly arranged for Mameha to take her in and raise her, holding back his own feelings out of loyalty to his friend Nobu. With Nobu's claim now released, the Chairman becomes Sayuri's patron and the great love of her life. In later years she leaves Japan for New York, where she opens a teahouse and lives out her days, recounting the whole of her story.

characters.description: Captain of the City Watch, hard-bitten and grudgingly staying sober, on the verge of retiring from the force to marry the noblewoman Lady Sybil Ramkin. A natural policeman who distrusts wealth and power even as he prepares to join them.
characters.name: Samuel Vimes

characters.description: The Watch's most popular member, a huge, good-natured young man raised by dwarfs who still treats every citizen as a neighbor and every law as sacred. His plain sincerity gives him a strange authority over people.
characters.name: Carrot Ironfoundersson

characters.description: The Watch's stout, cautious sergeant, a comfortable creature of habit who prefers a quiet patrol and a quiet life.
characters.name: Fred Colon

characters.description: The Watch's grubby, disreputable corporal, a small scrounger of uncertain ancestry whose instincts run to theft and self-preservation.
characters.name: Nobby Nobbs

characters.description: The cold, brilliant Patrician of Ankh-Morpork, who rules by balancing every faction against the others. He has no love for the Watch but understands exactly how useful, and how dangerous, it could become.
characters.name: Lord Vetinari

characters.description: Vimes's fiancee, a large-hearted, immensely wealthy noblewoman who breeds swamp dragons and is steadily drawing the reluctant captain into a comfortable, respectable life.
characters.name: Lady Sybil Ramkin

characters.description: One of the Watch's new recruits, taken on as the force is broadened to reflect the city's many peoples. A capable, watchful young woman who keeps the details of her background firmly to herself.
characters.name: Angua

characters.description: A troll newly recruited to the Watch, previously employed as a nightclub bouncer. Enormously strong and slow-witted in the warmth, he thinks far more clearly when the air turns cold.
characters.name: Detritus

characters.description: A dwarf recruited to the Watch alongside the troll Detritus, at first wary of his people's traditional enemy. Steady and practical, he brings a dwarf's eye for stone and detail to the work.
characters.name: Cuddy

characters.description: A young, impoverished member of the Assassins' Guild, obsessed with bloodlines and the vanished monarchy of Ankh-Morpork. Convinced the city has been diminished by the loss of its kings, he sets a dangerous plan in motion.
characters.name: Edward d'Eath

characters.description: The head of the Assassins' Guild, master of an institution that teaches killing as a refined profession. Formidable and self-controlled, he takes a close interest when a unique item goes missing from the Guild's museum.
characters.name: Dr Cruces

characters.description: A unique weapon held in the Assassins' Guild museum, the only one of its kind on the Disc, a device that kills at a distance with terrible ease. It seems to exert a will and a whispering influence over anyone who carries it.
characters.name: The Gonne

recaps.ending: The gonne passes from hand to hand, corrupting each holder, until it reaches Dr Cruces, the head of the Assassins' Guild, who is behind the killings. Carrot confronts and kills him, driving a sword clean through him, and the deadly weapon is destroyed so it can whisper to no one else. The investigation also confirms, with heraldic and physical proof, that Carrot is almost certainly the true heir to Ankh-Morpork's throne, and Carrot, wanting nothing to do with kingship, quietly sets the evidence aside and remains an ordinary officer, content to keep the pragmatic Vetinari in power. The cost is real: the dwarf recruit Cuddy is killed during the case. Angua's secret, that she is a werewolf, comes out, and she and Carrot grow close. Vimes marries Lady Sybil; instead of the quiet retirement he expected, Vetinari makes him Commander of the newly enlarged City Watch, now permanently staffed by trolls, dwarfs, a werewolf, and others, marking the Watch's transformation into a genuine force.
recaps.in_short: As Captain Vimes prepares to retire and marry Lady Sybil, the Ankh-Morpork City Watch is being expanded to include its first troll, dwarf, and a guarded young woman recruit named Angua. A one-of-a-kind weapon, the gonne, which can kill at a distance and whispers to whoever holds it, is stolen from the Assassins' Guild, and a string of killings follows. Edward d'Eath, an assassin obsessed with restoring the monarchy, believes Carrot is the rightful heir and means to use the gonne and the murders to force a king back onto the throne. The Watch investigates against the wishes of the Guilds and the Patrician. The weapon corrupts a series of hands until the Guild's own head, Dr Cruces, is wielding it. Carrot uncovers the truth, kills Cruces, and the gonne is destroyed. Presented with real proof of his royal descent, Carrot deliberately refuses the crown and stays a watchman. Vimes marries Sybil and, rather than retiring, is made Commander of a much larger Watch by Vetinari.

recaps.text: Previously, in Guards! Guards!: Ankh-Morpork's Night Watch had dwindled to a handful of hopeless men led by the drunken, cynical Captain Sam Vimes, alongside Sergeant Colon and Corporal Nobbs. The earnest, dwarf-raised recruit Carrot Ironfoundersson joined their ranks, and together they helped foil a secret brotherhood's plot to seize the city by summoning a dragon. In the aftermath the Watch regained a little respect, Vimes began courting the wealthy dragon-breeding noblewoman Lady Sybil Ramkin, and the Patrician, Lord Vetinari, remained the cold and calculating master of the city. A quiet suggestion was left unresolved: that Carrot may be of Ankh-Morpork's lost royal line.

Captain Vimes is only days from retiring to marry Lady Sybil, while the City Watch is being enlarged and opened up, awkwardly taking on its first troll, its first dwarf, and other recruits from the city's varied peoples, including a watchful young woman named Angua. As the changeover begins, a unique and dangerous object is stolen from the Assassins' Guild museum, and a young assassin obsessed with the city's lost kings quietly pursues a scheme of his own.

characters.description: The boy once known as Matt, now a few years older, living in a welcoming community simply called Village, which has long taken in outcasts and the damaged from harsher places. Energetic and good-hearted, he runs messages for the community and is one of the few people able to travel safely through the surrounding Forest. He longs to be given a true, grown-up name for his role, and he carries a secret he does not yet fully understand about himself.
characters.name: Matty

characters.description: A wise, gentle blind man who took Matty in and raised him in Village, and who is respected there for his insight and kindness. He is the father of Kira, a girl Matty knew in his old village, and he asks Matty to make a journey to bring her to him. Though he cannot see, he is one of the community's most clear-sighted and trusted members.
characters.name: Seer

characters.description: The young man who leads Village, marked by unusually pale eyes and by a rare gift for seeing beyond the ordinary. He arrived years earlier as a boy fleeing a rigidly controlled community, and he guides Village with wisdom and compassion. He is troubled as he watches something begin to change and darken among his people.
characters.name: Leader

characters.description: A young woman from a harsh distant village, born with a twisted leg and gifted with an extraordinary talent for weaving. She is the daughter of the blind man who raised Matty, and she once chose to stay behind in her own community to try to shape a better future there. Matty remembers her fondly from his childhood.
characters.name: Kira

characters.description: The respected schoolteacher of Village, a scholarly widower who has long been kind and generous to Matty and to the community's children. He is one of the older residents who remember when Village first opened its arms to strangers, and he becomes caught up in the unsettling changes spreading through the community.
characters.name: Mentor

characters.description: The strange, smooth figure who presides over a mysterious gathering called Trade Mart, where villagers can bargain for the things they secretly want. His trades come at a hidden and troubling cost, and his growing influence coincides with a hardening of hearts in a community that was once open and welcoming.
characters.name: Trademaster

recaps.ending: As Village grows cruel, corrupted by the bargains people make at Trade Mart, its people vote to seal the border against all newcomers, and the surrounding Forest turns malevolent, thickening and killing those who try to pass. Leader sends Matty on one last journey to fetch Kira before the closing. On the way back, the Forest attacks them savagely. Matty, who has recently discovered he can heal with his hands, realizes the only way to save Kira, and everyone who might still come to Village, is to heal the Forest and the poisoned land itself. He gives everything he has, pouring out his own life force into the ground. The healing succeeds: the Forest is cleansed, the corruption lifts, and the community's hardened hearts begin to soften. But the effort costs Matty his life, and he dies with Kira and Leader beside him. In recognition of his final act, he is given the true name he had always wanted, Healer. Village reopens, mourning the boy whose sacrifice restored it.
recaps.in_short: In the welcoming community called Village, which has long taken in outcasts, a boy named Matty carries messages and travels safely through the surrounding Forest. He was raised by a wise blind man, Seer, the father of his old friend Kira, and the community is guided by Leader, a young man with pale eyes and the gift of seeing beyond. But Village is changing: through a mysterious Trade Mart run by the sinister Trademaster, people bargain away their better selves for shallow wants, growing selfish and cruel, until they vote to wall out all newcomers. As their hearts darken, the once-gentle Forest turns deadly and begins to attack travelers. Leader sends Matty to bring Kira to Village before the border closes. Returning through the now-lethal Forest with Kira, Matty discovers he has a rare gift for healing. When the poisoned Forest threatens to kill them, Matty pours out his life to heal the Forest itself, dying in the effort. His sacrifice cleanses the land and breaks the community's cruelty, and he is honored at last with a true name.

recaps.text: Earlier in the series: In a rigidly controlled community that had abolished memory, pain, color, and choice, a boy named Jonas was chosen to hold the society's suppressed memories. Learning the truth about his world, he fled with a baby to save its life and came at last to a gentler place. In a separate, harsh village, an orphaned girl named Kira, born with a twisted leg and gifted at weaving, uncovered the lies of her own community's rulers, was reunited with the blind father she had thought dead, and chose to stay and work for change; her scrappy young friend Matt was the boy who had helped her. Now Jonas leads a welcoming community called Village, the blind man lives there and has raised Matt, and Matt has grown into the messenger of this story.

Matty lives in Village, a community founded to welcome outcasts and the wounded from crueler places, and works as its messenger, one of the few able to pass safely through the surrounding Forest. He was raised by Seer, the wise blind man who is Kira's father, and the community is led by Leader, a young man with pale eyes and a gift for seeing beyond the ordinary. Matty hopes to earn a true grown-up name for his work. But something is beginning to change in Village and in the Forest around it, and the openness that has always defined the community is starting to falter.

characters.description: A sixteen-year-old university student whose intelligence has drawn the direct attention of Morganville's Founder. Claire's new protection bracelet makes most vampires keep their distance, but it also means Amelie can require her to undertake secret and dangerous work.
characters.name: Claire Danvers

characters.description: Claire's boyfriend and housemate. Shane survived a death sentence and his father's failed war on Morganville, but Michael's transformation has placed a vampire inside the circle he considers family, testing both his temper and his loyalty.
characters.name: Shane Collins

characters.description: Claire's Goth housemate and closest female friend. Eve loves Michael but is adjusting to his new vampirism, and the return of her troubled younger brother Jason brings old family fear into Glass House.
characters.name: Eve Rosser

characters.description: The owner of Glass House, recently transformed from a ghostlike being into a vampire. Michael can finally leave the property and pursue his music, but he must manage blood hunger while preserving his relationships with Eve, Shane, and Claire.
characters.name: Michael Glass

characters.description: Morganville's ancient Founder and Claire's new patron. Amelie assigns Claire to work on a secret problem threatening the town's vampires, offering protection while revealing little about the risks or the fate of earlier assistants.
characters.name: Amelie

characters.description: An ancient vampire scholar suffering from a disease that causes confusion, paranoia, and violent loss of control. Myrnin is brilliant enough to seek a cure for the illness afflicting Morganville's vampires, but teaching Claire in his hidden laboratory makes him both her mentor and an immediate danger.
characters.name: Myrnin

characters.description: Eve's younger brother, newly returned to Morganville. Jason is angry, unpredictable, and fascinated by vampire violence; Eve knows enough of his past to fear what his presence may mean as attacks on young women spread through town.
characters.name: Jason Rosser

characters.description: Claire's university enemy, now forced to recognize that the Founder's bracelet gives Claire unusual status. Monica remains vindictive, but Amelie's orders sometimes require her to help Claire move through dangers that threaten them both.
characters.name: Monica Morrell

characters.description: Michael's grandfather and a vampire who remains unusually close to his human sympathies. Sam helps Michael adjust to his transformation and supports Claire as she learns why Amelie is so desperate for Myrnin's research to succeed.
characters.name: Sam Glass

characters.description: The vampire owner of Common Grounds and Amelie's rival. Oliver understands the danger posed by the vampires' illness and cooperates when Morganville itself is threatened, without giving up his ambition to challenge the Founder.
characters.name: Oliver

characters.description: An ancient and commanding vampire who arrives in Morganville with Ysandre and François. Bishop is Amelie's father and treats her town as a place he can enter and dominate, making his appearance a direct threat to the existing order and to Glass House.
characters.name: Bishop

characters.description: A dangerous vampire who arrives in Morganville as part of Bishop's entourage. Ysandre combines polished manners with open contempt for the young residents of Glass House.
characters.name: Ysandre

characters.description: One of the vampires accompanying Bishop into Morganville. François helps enforce Bishop's authority when the visitors confront the residents of Glass House.
characters.name: François

recaps.ending: Claire's work with Myrnin produces a treatment that can restore some of his clarity, but it is not a permanent cure for the disease destroying vampire memory and self-control. Myrnin remains dangerous, the research must continue, and Claire is now too important to Amelie's plans to step away. The attacks on young women are tied to Jason Rosser, confirming Eve's fear that her brother brought lethal violence back into her life; the Glass House residents survive his immediate threat, but the damage to Eve and the household remains. Michael continues adapting to vampirism while he, Eve, Shane, and Claire recommit to protecting one another. Before this fragile stability can last, an ancient vampire named Bishop arrives with Ysandre and François. Bishop is revealed as Amelie's father and asserts himself at Glass House with no respect for Amelie's arrangements. His arrival introduces a power older than the town's current order and leaves Claire and her friends facing a new invasion from within vampire society.
recaps.in_short: Protected but now personally bound to Amelie, Claire is ordered to study with Myrnin, an ancient vampire scientist whose mind is failing from a disease spreading among Morganville's vampires. His hidden work may produce a cure, yet his violent lapses make every lesson dangerous. At Glass House, Michael adjusts to life as a vampire, his romance with Eve and friendship with Shane remain strained, and Eve's disturbed brother Jason returns as young women are attacked. Claire balances university, Myrnin's research, and the threat closing around her friends. She helps develop a treatment that gives Myrnin periods of clarity but does not cure the underlying illness. Jason's connection to the killings is exposed and his immediate threat to the household is stopped. Any relief is brief: Bishop, an ancient vampire and Amelie's father, arrives with two powerful companions and forces his presence upon Glass House. His entrance threatens Amelie's authority and leaves Claire's household at the edge of a much larger conflict.

recaps.text: Previously: Claire Danvers moved into Glass House with Eve Rosser, Shane Collins, and Michael Glass after discovering that vampires rule Morganville. Michael had been killed by a vampire but preserved by the house in a ghostlike state. Shane's father Frank then invaded with armed vampire hunters, whose killing of Brandon led the authorities to arrest and sentence Shane to death. Claire, Eve, and their allies stopped Frank's wider attack and saved Shane. To leave the house and join the rescue, Michael accepted Amelie's offer to transform him into a vampire. He is now physically free but must adjust to the change, while Eve and Shane struggle with what it means. Claire also accepted the protection of Amelie, Morganville's Founder. The bracelet that guards her from lesser vampires marks her as Amelie's subject and gives the Founder the right to call on Claire's unusual intelligence.

Life at Glass House has changed. Michael can leave at any hour now that he is a vampire, but blood hunger and the reactions of his friends complicate his new freedom. Eve loves him while fearing the distance his transformation may create, and Shane's hatred of vampires makes friendship with Michael difficult. Claire's gold bracelet prevents casual vampire attacks and changes the way Monica treats her, but it is also a visible reminder that Amelie owns her service. The Founder summons Claire for a confidential assignment suited to her scientific ability. At the same time, reports of attacks on young women unsettle the town, adding a human-scale danger to the secret demands Claire is not yet permitted to explain to her housemates.

Amelie sends Claire to a hidden laboratory to study with Myrnin, an ancient vampire scientist. Myrnin is brilliant, erratic, and suffering from an illness that destroys memory and restraint; during bad periods he may attack the person trying to help him. His research seeks a treatment for the same disease in Morganville's vampire population, explaining why Amelie is willing to risk Claire and why the work must remain secret. Claire begins sorting through his methods and records while learning procedures meant to keep her alive during his lapses. Outside the laboratory, Eve's younger brother Jason returns to town. He is volatile and obsessed with vampires, and Eve responds with fear rather than relief. As violence against young women continues, his presence puts new pressure on Glass House just as Claire's secrecy about Myrnin separates her from the friends who normally protect her.

Claire continues her dangerous apprenticeship, using her scientific training to give structure to Myrnin's disordered work. She learns that the vampires' illness is not an isolated case: it threatens the stability of Morganville, and even Amelie and Oliver need the research to succeed. Myrnin can be lucid and generous one moment and predatory the next, so progress never makes the laboratory safe. Sam Glass helps Claire and Michael understand the stakes while Michael works to control his vampire nature and preserve his relationship with Eve. The attacks around town draw suspicion toward Jason, whose behavior confirms that he is concealing something. Eve is torn between the knowledge of what her brother can do and the burden of bringing danger upon him if she speaks. Claire's obligations now pull her between protecting a failing vampire who may kill her and identifying the threat stalking people close to home.

The evidence around the attacks increasingly ties Jason to the violence, forcing Eve and the Glass House residents to treat him as a danger rather than merely a damaged relative. Claire faces threats from both Jason's actions and Myrnin's worsening instability. Her work nevertheless produces a promising treatment that can restore some of Myrnin's memory and control. The improvement is temporary rather than a cure, leaving Claire essential to a research program she never freely chose. Michael, Shane, and Eve work through enough of their tension to protect one another when the separate dangers converge. Amelie's secrecy and Oliver's interest make clear that a struggle over the disease's treatment could also become a struggle over who controls Morganville.

Claire and her friends survive the immediate danger surrounding Jason, whose involvement in the attacks on young women confirms Eve's worst fears about her brother. Myrnin receives a treatment that gives him periods of clarity, but the underlying vampire illness remains unsolved and he is still capable of violent relapse. Claire therefore remains bound to both the research and Amelie's service. Michael continues building a life as a vampire without abandoning Eve, Shane, or Claire, and the four residents hold Glass House together despite the strain. Their fragile recovery ends when three unfamiliar vampires arrive: Bishop, Ysandre, and François. Bishop is an ancient, forceful vampire and Amelie's father. He enters Morganville as though its existing protections and its Founder have no authority over him, confronting Glass House and taking an interest in its residents. The book closes with Bishop's arrival threatening Amelie's rule and placing Claire's household at the front of a new conflict.

characters.description: A powerful Elemental who has resumed working with Skulduggery after five years away. Valkyrie remains affected by panic, guilt, and the legacy of Darquesse, but her younger sister Alice gives her a connection to ordinary family life that she is determined to protect.
characters.name: Valkyrie Cain

characters.description: A skeleton detective and Valkyrie's long-time partner. Skulduggery is hunting the newly restored Abyssinia and the surviving Anti-Sanctuary while trying to support Valkyrie without allowing concern for her to slow the investigation.
characters.name: Skulduggery Pleasant

characters.description: Valkyrie's much younger sister, who knows her as Stephanie and is largely sheltered from the magical conflicts surrounding the family. Alice is open, affectionate, and central to Valkyrie's hope that at least one part of her home life can remain safe.
characters.name: Alice Edgley

characters.description: An insecure Corrival Academy student who recently helped Skulduggery and Valkyrie expose the Anti-Sanctuary's reach into the school. Omen remains overshadowed by his brother Auger, but continues to become involved when events demand courage rather than prestige.
characters.name: Omen Darkly

characters.description: Omen's Teleporter friend at Corrival Academy. Never is socially confident, changeable in gender presentation, and usually quicker than Omen to understand the shifting loyalties and relationships around them.
characters.name: Never

characters.description: Omen's older brother and the Chosen One expected to kill the King of the Darklands. Auger's talent and public destiny make him the focus of Corrival Academy, although he remains personally protective of Omen.
characters.name: Auger Darkly

characters.description: The resurrected leader of the Anti-Sanctuary, restored from her preserved heart. Abyssinia possesses immense power and a personal history with Skulduggery, and she is now pursuing family concerns as well as the wider ambitions of her followers.
characters.name: Abyssinia

characters.description: A Neoteric killer whose control over any place he considers home allows him to change its dimensions and rules. Cadaverous has left Abyssinia's service with a grievance and selects Valkyrie's family as the means of forcing her into a contest on his terms.
characters.name: Cadaverous Gant

characters.description: The Supreme Mage governing Roarhaven and the Irish Sanctuary. China is attempting to maintain control while Abyssinia's return exposes both political weaknesses and secrets rooted in the sorcerers' long history.
characters.name: China Sorrows

characters.description: A Sanctuary operative and teacher who continues to watch events at Corrival Academy. Temper gives Omen practical support and serves as a link between the students and the adults pursuing Abyssinia's organization.
characters.name: Temper Fray

characters.description: A masked organizer of the Darquesse Society. Sebastian is convinced that Darquesse must be returned to the world and quietly recruits people willing to help him reach her, without explaining the source of his certainty.
characters.name: Sebastian Tao

characters.description: A powerful and psychologically damaged sorcerer whom Abyssinia identifies as her lost son. Caisson has spent years confined and abused, making his recovery both the most personal part of her campaign and a source of fresh danger.
characters.name: Caisson

recaps.ending: Valkyrie reaches Alice before Cadaverous Gant's deadline and survives the shifting territory in which his home-based magic gives him control. Gant dies in the final confrontation, ending his attempt to punish Valkyrie through her sister. Alice is brought home alive, but the ordeal leaves Valkyrie confronting the older fear she has kept hidden: Alice's soul was not restored whole after Darquesse killed her years earlier. Saving Alice physically has therefore not solved the deeper damage. Skulduggery and Valkyrie also fail to end Abyssinia's campaign. Abyssinia reaches Caisson, the son she has been seeking, and removes him from the confinement in which he has spent years. She now has both her restored power and the family member at the centre of her plans. Omen remains connected to the detectives, while Sebastian Tao continues assembling the Darquesse Society for an attempted return of Darquesse.
recaps.in_short: With Abyssinia active after her resurrection, Skulduggery and Valkyrie try to trace her plans while Omen Darkly continues navigating Corrival Academy. Cadaverous Gant, a former Anti-Sanctuary operative whose magic gives him control inside his home, turns the conflict into a personal ordeal. He kidnaps Valkyrie's little sister Alice and gives Valkyrie until midnight to find her, driving her through a sequence of traps and distorted spaces. Valkyrie reaches Alice and Gant dies in the confrontation, but the rescue exposes the deeper problem Valkyrie has feared since the Darquesse crisis: Alice is alive without a complete soul. Elsewhere, Abyssinia succeeds in reaching Caisson, the damaged son she has long sought, and takes him from confinement. The immediate kidnapping is over, but Valkyrie must now find a way to make Alice whole while Abyssinia's restored family gives the larger enemy campaign new momentum.

recaps.text: Five years after Darquesse's defeat, Valkyrie Cain returned to Ireland from a self-imposed exile marked by guilt, depression, and recurring trauma. She resumed her partnership with Skulduggery and helped investigate the Anti-Sanctuary, with assistance from overlooked Corrival Academy student Omen Darkly. They freed Skulduggery after the Neoteric Smoke corrupted his judgment, but failed to stop the enemy's main objective. The healer Melior was forced to rebuild the powerful sorcerer Abyssinia from her preserved heart, and she escaped alive with her followers. Valkyrie stayed in Ireland rather than withdrawing again. Her little sister Alice remains the most important part of her family life, while Valkyrie privately carries fear about the consequences of Alice's death and restoration during the earlier Darquesse crisis.

Skulduggery and Valkyrie pursue signs of Abyssinia and the remnants of the Anti-Sanctuary, whose leader now has a living body and the freedom to act. Valkyrie is back in the field but has not recovered from the anxiety and guilt that controlled her years away. Her relationship with her young sister Alice remains a refuge from that life. At Corrival Academy, Omen continues to be overlooked beside his brother Auger, yet his earlier service to the detectives means that danger and responsibility no longer pass him by entirely. Abyssinia's activities suggest that her immediate priority is not a public attack but the recovery of someone connected to her past.

Cadaverous Gant, no longer content to serve as one of Abyssinia's operatives, acts on his grievance against Valkyrie. He abducts Alice and establishes a deadline at midnight, forcing Valkyrie to follow the path he has prepared if she wants her sister returned alive. Gant's Neoteric discipline makes any place he accepts as home into his territory: within it he can stretch distance, alter surroundings, and make ordinary escape impossible. Skulduggery searches for ways to reach Valkyrie and Alice, but Gant has designed the contest to isolate Valkyrie and use her fear for her family against her.

Valkyrie follows Gant's trail through escalating traps, knowing that every delay brings Alice closer to the deadline. The distorted spaces under Gant's control turn the rescue into a contest of endurance as well as magic, and Valkyrie's existing trauma makes his psychological pressure especially effective. Separate from the kidnapping, Omen and Never continue dealing with the consequences of the Anti-Sanctuary's influence at Corrival Academy. Sebastian Tao also advances his quiet effort to gather a society dedicated to finding Darquesse, convinced that her return will eventually be necessary.

As midnight approaches, Valkyrie penetrates further into the environment Gant controls and closes the distance to Alice. Gant's advantage depends on treating the battleground as his home, so direct strength alone cannot defeat him; Valkyrie must survive rules he can change while keeping her attention on the hostage rather than his provocations. At the same time, Skulduggery's pursuit of Abyssinia reveals that the resurrected sorcerer's search centres on Caisson, a son who has spent years imprisoned and psychologically damaged. Even if Alice is recovered, Abyssinia is close to achieving the family reunion that motivates this stage of her campaign.

Valkyrie reaches Alice before the deadline and the sisters survive Gant's final trap. Cadaverous Gant dies in the confrontation, ending his private campaign and allowing Alice to return to her family. The rescue does not resolve everything Valkyrie fears about her sister. Alice's soul was restored incompletely after Darquesse killed her years ago, and Valkyrie now has to face the damage rather than merely keep it secret. Meanwhile, Abyssinia reaches Caisson and takes her long-confined son with her, strengthening the personal core of her movement. Skulduggery and Valkyrie therefore end the night with Alice alive but with both a new quest to make her whole and Abyssinia's continuing threat ahead of them. Sebastian's plan to recover Darquesse also remains in motion.

characters.description: The narrator of this retelling, a vampire who has spent decades posing as a high-school student in the small, rainy town of Forks with his adopted family, the Cullens. More than a century old but forever seventeen in appearance, he is telepathic, able to hear the thoughts of everyone around him, and he and his family abstain from human blood, hunting only animals. When a new human girl, Bella Swan, arrives at school, he is thrown into crisis: hers is the one mind he cannot read, and her scent is more powerfully, dangerously tempting to him than any he has known. Cultured, guarded, and tormented by what he is, he struggles between the pull to destroy her and an unwilling fascination.
characters.name: Edward Cullen

characters.description: A seventeen-year-old who has just moved from Phoenix to live with her father in Forks. Seen through Edward's eyes, she is quiet, observant, and unexpectedly hard to predict: her thoughts are silent to him, which unnerves and intrigues him, and her blood calls to him with unbearable force. Modest and often self-conscious, she seems drawn to Edward despite his coldness, unafraid in a way that both frustrates and captivates him.
characters.name: Bella Swan

characters.description: The compassionate physician who leads the Cullen family and long ago turned Edward and several of the others. Centuries old and remarkably self-controlled, he works at the Forks hospital surrounded by human blood and holds firmly to a life of restraint and mercy. He is a calm, fatherly figure whose conscience shapes the whole family's way of living.
characters.name: Carlisle Cullen

characters.description: Carlisle's wife and the warm, nurturing mother of the Cullen household. Gentle and loving, she is devoted to her adopted children and quietly hopes for Edward's happiness, having watched him remain apart and alone for decades.
characters.name: Esme Cullen

characters.description: One of Edward's adopted sisters, a small, quick, cheerful vampire who can see glimpses of the future, though what she sees can change as people's choices change. Fond of Edward and unusually open-minded, she foresees possibilities involving Bella that startle and unsettle him.
characters.name: Alice Cullen

characters.description: Alice's mate and a member of the Cullen family, a lean, watchful vampire who can sense and influence the emotions of those around him. Newer than the others to their diet of animal blood, he finds the restraint the hardest to keep, and the presence of a tempting human strains him most.
characters.name: Jasper Hale

characters.description: The biggest and most powerfully built of the Cullen siblings, Rosalie's mate, boisterous and good-humored. He treats life lightly and is fond of physical strength and contests, and he regards Edward's sudden turmoil over a human girl with easygoing amusement.
characters.name: Emmett Cullen

characters.description: The strikingly beautiful blonde among the Cullen siblings, Emmett's mate. Proud and resentful of the risk a human outsider poses to the family's secret and safety, she strongly objects to Edward's growing interest in Bella and makes her hostility plain.
characters.name: Rosalie Hale

characters.description: Bella's father and the police chief of Forks, a quiet, undemonstrative man who has lived alone for years and is glad, if awkward, to have his daughter back. He is largely unaware of the danger gathering around her, and his ordinary human concern for Bella becomes another thing Edward must work around.
characters.name: Charlie Swan

characters.description: A younger teenager from the Quileute reservation at La Push, son of an old friend of Bella's father. Cheerful and talkative, he is connected to the tribe's old legends about the Cullens' kind, folklore that carries a warning the Cullens take seriously because of a long-standing pact between the two peoples.
characters.name: Jacob Black

characters.description: A nomadic vampire who arrives near Forks with two companions, all three of whom hunt humans. Lean and unremarkable to look at, he is a gifted and relentless tracker who treats pursuit as a game. When he senses the Cullens guarding a human, he becomes fixed on hunting Bella for the sheer challenge of it.
characters.name: James

characters.description: A vivid red-haired vampire who travels with James as his mate. Wary and feline in her movements, she stands with him and helps him when he sets out to hunt Bella.
characters.name: Victoria

characters.description: The most civil-seeming of the three nomad vampires, dark-skinned and courteous, who speaks for the group when they meet the Cullens. Uneasy about the conflict James is starting, he chooses to part from his companions rather than take part in the hunt.
characters.name: Laurent

recaps.ending: Edward reaches Bella in a Phoenix ballet studio after James has bitten her, and the Cullens destroy the tracker. Bella's greatest peril then becomes the vampire venom spreading in her blood: rather than let her change, Edward forces himself to draw the venom out through the bite, mastering the very thirst that first tempted him and stopping himself before he drains her. She survives, badly injured but still human, and wakes in a hospital where Edward has arranged a cover story for her worried father. The two return to Forks and to their life at school, and Edward takes her to the prom, deflecting for now her wish to become a vampire and stay with him forever. James is dead, but his mate, the red-haired Victoria, has slipped away, and Edward knows the reprieve is uneasy. The book closes with Edward and Bella together, deeply in love, still shadowed by the constant threat that his nature, and the vampire world, pose to a fragile human girl.
recaps.in_short: Midnight Sun retells the events of Twilight from Edward Cullen's point of view. Edward is a telepathic vampire hiding among humans in Forks with his family, who feed only on animals. When Bella Swan arrives at school, he is stunned that he cannot hear her thoughts and nearly undone by how strongly her blood tempts him. He fights to stay away from her, then to protect her, as the two fall in love against his every instinct and the danger he poses. After he saves her from a speeding van and later from an attacker, he tells her what he is; she accepts it. He brings her to meet his family, but a passing trio of human-hunting nomads arrives during a family baseball game, and one of them, a tracker named James, fixes on hunting Bella for sport. The Cullens flee with her, but James lures her away and bites her. Edward destroys James and, in an agony of self-control, sucks the venom from her wound to keep her human, saving her life without turning her. Bella recovers, and they return to their fragile life together in Forks, the danger of what Edward is still hanging over them.

recaps.text: Edward Cullen, a telepathic vampire posing as a teenager in Forks with his adopted family, is thrown off balance when a new student, Bella Swan, arrives: he cannot hear her thoughts, and her scent tempts him more than any human's ever has. In a biology class he is nearly overwhelmed by the urge to kill her and barely holds himself back, then leaves town for several days to regain control. Returning, he resolves to keep his distance, but when a van skids across the icy school parking lot toward Bella, he moves with impossible speed to shield her, stopping the vehicle with his hand. Bella notices what should have been impossible and begins to suspect he is not ordinary. Fascinated against his will and unable to stay away, Edward finds himself drawn ever closer to the one person whose mind is silent to him.

Edward and Bella circle each other warily, each intensely curious about the other. When Bella wanders into danger from a group of men in nearby Port Angeles, Edward, tracking her through the minds around her, arrives in time to rescue her, and afterward admits that he can read thoughts, though not hers. Their fascination deepens into love even as Edward warns her how dangerous he is. He finally confirms to her what he and his family are, showing her the truth of himself, and is amazed that she is not repelled but accepts him. His family reacts with unease: some fear the risk a knowing human poses to their secret, and Rosalie in particular objects, while Alice's visions suggest that Bella's future may be bound tightly to theirs. Edward, long solitary among his own kind, lets himself hope.

Edward brings Bella home to meet the Cullens, and most of the family welcomes her. During a thunderstorm the family gathers to play baseball, their strength and speed unleashed, but the game is interrupted by three passing vampires, nomads who hunt humans: James, Victoria, and Laurent. James, a tracker who treats hunting as a game, catches Bella's scent among the Cullens and instantly makes her his quarry. Laurent, uneasy, leaves the others rather than join the chase, but James will not be turned aside. To protect Bella, the Cullens scatter and set decoys: Edward and some of the family try to draw James away while Alice and Jasper take Bella into hiding in her old home city of Phoenix. The hunt tightens, and Edward is desperate to keep the danger he brought into her life from destroying her.

James outwits the Cullens' protection by tricking Bella into believing he has captured her mother, luring her to a ballet studio in Phoenix, where he attacks and bites her. Edward and his family arrive and destroy James, but the venom already in Bella's blood threatens to turn her into a vampire. In an act of extreme self-mastery, Edward draws the venom out through the wound, forcing himself to stop before he drains her, and saves her life while keeping her human. Bella recovers in a hospital, her injuries explained away to her father with a cover story, and she and Edward return to Forks. He takes her to the school prom, gently resisting, for now, her desire to be changed so she can stay with him forever. James is gone, but his mate Victoria has escaped, leaving a lingering threat. The book ends with Edward and Bella together and in love, still shadowed by the dangers of what he is.
